- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline at 10% below peak or align with 20-day moving average.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, model overreacts to negative sentiment — dampen forecast drop by 2–3%.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops in 10–15 day horizons when sentiment is negative — add 2–4% buffer to forecast for negative sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5), model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–3% for 15+ day forecasts.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — use 20-day EWMA to smooth out sentiment-driven noise.
